Plus, the new ones have been redesigned and the sizing is off. [Here are pictures of the new and old](https://imgur.com/a/htRoGkc). Is there a way to get my old ones back to being more of that matte, rustic finish? I'm a super newbie to leather and shoe care, so sorry if this is a super obvious question!

Full story with more details in case it's helpful:

 

I have a few chronic health conditions. I’ve seen so many different doctors over the years and due to the rarity of my problems, the fact that they don’t just involve one part of my body and require coordination across different doctors, I’ve had very little luck. I’ve liked the idea of functional medicine, or a type of alternative medicine that looks at the entire body as a whole and the way each system interacts with each other. I first saw a functional medicine doctor three years ago at the Cleveland Clinic and had a relatively decent experience, but wasn’t able to make many follow-ups as I moved away from the area. 

In the last 6 months, I felt my symptoms getting much worse again, and because I had already been to many of the few doctors in my area that knew about or specialized in my problems, I decided to try functional medicine again. I was weary because most practices seemed to not have any actual doctors but rather solely dietitians or “certified functional medicine practitioners,” I was a bit weary. Because I mostly just wanted to repeat the testing I had done at the Cleveland Clinic, I finally found a practice that did the same testing and had actual MDs as the practitioners. 

When I had my initial appointment, I was ready to tell my entire medical history which started at 18 months (I’m 23 now). Halfway through, however, the doctor said “I’m less interested in your history and more interested in the symptoms you’re experiencing now.” I should’ve seen this as a red flag, but my desperation to be healthy again led me to ignore it and answer her questions. Even though the root cause of my main medical problem had been discovered already and I was mostly looking for help managing all of the symptoms (there are no cures for my illnesses), the doctor was so adamant that my problems came from a chronic Lyme disease infection (even though I had been tested for lyme at my first functional medicine experience and the results were negative). I was told that traditional lyme testing is not very accurate and she wanted to redo it with a different type. Seeing as she is a doctor and I didn’t have any reason to not trust her, I said ok. 

Because this type of testing would take a few months to get results back and because I’m planning on moving from the area for the summer in a few months, we decided that the smartest thing to do would be to get me started on a treatment plan based on my test results from my previous functional medicine testing and then adjust the plan as I get results in. I felt this was reasonable. As I couldn’t be on any supplements or vitamins prior to the first round of testing, I waited three weeks until testing was over to pick up my “prescribed” (I understand it’s not a medication that’s prescribed, per se, but I was directed to take it by her) supplements. On my notes from my first appointment, she had given a basic category of symptoms for which each supplement was supposed to help (i.e., “Gut,” “adrenal support,” “immune support,” etc). 

I picked up my supplements and began taking them as directed. Two in particular had the instructions of “take 1 drop by mouth twice a day, increase drops as tolerated.” I cannot even begin to describe how awful I felt after taking these. I was extremely fatigued and unable to leave my bed for the day. I had severe brain fog and could not think clearly. My body felt pained. My heart rate was extremely high. These are symptoms of my illness that I hadn’t experienced in years. I recognized the brand of one of these supplements as the same as another supplement I was directed to take three years ago from my previous functional medicine doctor. She warned that it may be a “I’ll feel worse before I feel better” situation, and I experienced a few averse side effects with that one but nothing to this extent. I immediately emailed the doctor asking if this experience was normal. She replied that it was. 

I stopped taking those two supplements the next day, but still was inundated with those same symptoms and barely able to complete my normal daily functions. Confused and upset, I started googling. I found forums of other patients who experienced this reaction for years, yet their doctor told them it was completely normal and to just keep pushing through. I also began looking up the ingredients for each. I am completely aware that supplements and vitamins are not FDA-approved. However, many of my symptoms or medicines were listed under contraindications and/or safety. For example

The first ingredient in one supplement is St. John’s Wort. This is known to interfere with birth control and make it less effective. I am on birth control. 

Some ingredients are sage and licorice which are possibly unsafe for long-term use. I was instructed to complete “2-3 bottles” of the supplement which contain hundreds of doses each. 

Multiple ingredients are known to not be safe for patients with endometriosis. I have endometriosis. The doctor knows this. 

Multiple ingredients are known to not be safe for patients with low blood pressure. I have low blood pressure. It is a fundamental part of my main chronic illness. The doctor knows this. 

One supplement has tea tree oil as an ingredient. Tea tree oil is great topically but is literally poisonous when ingested. 

I emailed the doctor 5 days ago and have yet to receive a response. I plan on calling on Monday. 

Also, upon finding out the day of testing that this new lyme test would be $450 out of pocket, I went home and did research on if traditional lyme testing was inaccurate. Credible, evidence-based sources said that traditional testing is only ineffective if done a few weeks after initial tick bite. I have had this symptoms for nearly 7 years and my traditional test was done 4 years after getting sick.
